summaryZh: 本文介绍了自主灌溉机器人360 Rain从单纯的雨水收集灌溉设备演变为高效粪肥和养分施用平台的过程。该系统通过GPS自主导航、3000英尺软管和精准根区施用技术，可将液态粪肥、沼液等与灌溉水混合后直接施入作物根区，节水40%，减少养分流失，使粪肥养分利用率大幅提升。目前50%-60%的设备用于奶牛和养猪场，覆盖美国40个州和加拿大，投资回收期2-4年。
featuredReason: 该文展示了自主机器人如何将灌溉与液态粪肥精准施用结合，实现水肥一体化根区施用，对养猪场和奶牛场的粪污资源化利用及种养结合具有重要参考价值，其节水40%、养分利用率翻倍的数据值得智慧畜牧从业者关注。

The rainmaker: Spoon-feeding water and manure

Asked and Answered: Learn how an idea for an autonomous irrigation machine, 360 Rain, became a highly efficient manure and nutrient applicator.

Holly Spangler,Prairie Farmer editor, Farm Progress executive editor,Prairie FarmerSeptember 25, 2026

The idea behind the 360 Rain machine was fairly straightforward: catch excess rain in one place, and use an autonomous machine to apply it directly to a crop’s root zone exactly when needed.

But like a lot of good ideas, this one evolved.

Today, most 360 Rain machines also apply liquid fertilizer like boron, sulfur or micronutrients, or liquid manure. They band it right into the root zone, mixed with water.

“We can be very efficient with those nutrients,” said Loren Weaver, eastern U.S. sales manager for 360 Rain, adding that 50% to 60% of their machines are currently used on dairy and hog operations. Nearly every machine is applying some kind of nutrient with the water.

The 360 Rain system is designed to apply water and nutrients directly to a plant’s roots, as needed. “We can be very efficient with that water,” said Loren Weaver, 360 Rain eastern U.S. sales manager. (Holly Spangler)

The machine carries 3,000 feet of 3-inch hose and can cover 200 acres from a single hookup point, which means it can irrigate odd-shaped fields where center pivots won’t work as well. The company claims 360 Rain uses 40% less water than a pivot, because it doesn’t lose water to evaporation.

Related:How strip tillage turned one farmer from skeptic to believer

The machine doesn’t actually turn around at the end rows; it reverses direction, backing up on the same pass and picking up its hose along the way. It operates autonomously using GPS technology, based on how the field was recorded during planting. It can run 24/7 for up to 30 days on a single fuel tank.

“The machine is designed to fit inside 30-inch rows, so it’ll intersect each planter pass and travel both ways off of that backbone to be able to cover 100% of the field,” Weaver said.

It takes about three and a half days for the machine to apply just under a half-inch of water across an 80-acre field, figuring a pump rate of 200 gallons per minute and about 977,000 gallons of water.

Weaver reported that the company has machines across 40 states and Canada, with more concentration through the dairy pockets of Ohio, Indiana and Wisconsin. (360 Rain)

Weaver described the 360 Rain machine as an “adaptive application system” that can be used on any crop, applying everything from dairy and hog manure to digestate and leachate.

“Any of those products can be mixed in the water stream and applied,” he said, adding that both water and nutrients can be applied at variable rates.

Return on investment

In general, Weaver said the machine creates an average 40-to-60-bushel yield increase, depending on location and soil type. A lighter soil or a sandy, drought-prone soil will respond even more dramatically than a heavier soil in a region with regular rainfall. He’s found that even farther north, where there is less traditional irrigation, farmers can still gain a lot of yield.

“Look at Borderview Farms in southern Michigan. One side of his field was lighter soil, and the other side was heavier. The lighter side, he got an 87-bushel increase, and on the heavier soil, he got about a 42-bushel increase,” Weaver said.

Related:‘Can’t do without it’: How to maximize nitrogen application

The company claims its 360 Rain machine uses 40% less water than a pivot, because it doesn’t lose water to evaporation. (360 Rain)

Base price for the machine is over $200,000, and Weaver estimates farmers will achieve return on investment in two to four years if they’re applying manure. With only irrigation and nutrient application, it may take five years.

And of course, the product makes the difference. The machine is particularly effective when applying hog manure, and returns are significant when nutrients are so readily available. Weaver said they’ve seen “really, really good results” when they spoon-feed a crop with four or five applications of hog manure throughout the growing season, along with water.

“Compare that to applying, say, 4,000 gallons per acre of hog manure in the fall. Come springtime, you’re only going to have about half of the nutrients available to the crop,” he explained.

That means the machine also reduces nutrient loss into water sources, and it makes for especially efficient water use, applying the water directly to the roots as needed. Farmers can also tissue sample weekly throughout the growing season and tweak the fertilizer mixtures accordingly.

360 Rain machines are available through local dealers.

About the Author

Holly Spangler

Prairie Farmer editor, Farm Progress executive editor, Prairie Farmer

Holly Spangler has covered Illinois agriculture for over 25 years, bringing meaningful production agriculture experience to the magazine’s coverage. She currently serves as editor of Prairie Farmer magazine and executive editor for Farm Progress, managing editorial staff at six publications across the Corn Belt.

A University of Illinois agricultural communications graduate and award-winning writer and photographer, Holly is past president of the American Agricultural Editors Association. In 2015, she became only the 10th U.S. agricultural journalist to earn the Writer of Merit designation and is a five-time winner of the top writing award for editorial opinion in U.S. agriculture. She is an AAEA Master Writer and was one of 10 recipients worldwide to receive the IFAJ-Alltech Young Leaders in Ag Journalism award. She serves on the Illinois 4-H Foundation and the Illinois Council on Ag Education. Her work in agricultural media has been recognized by the Illinois Soybean Association, Illinois Corn, Illinois Society of Professional Farm Managers and Rural Appraisers, and more.

Holly and her husband, John, farm in western Illinois where they raise corn, soybeans and beef cattle on 2,500 acres. Their operation includes 125 head of commercial cows in a cow/calf operation. Locally, she serves on the school board and volunteers with 4-H and FFA.

translationZh:
360 Rain机器背后的想法相当简单：在一个地方收集多余的雨水，然后使用自主机器在需要时直接将水施用到作物的根区。

但就像许多好主意一样，这个想法也在不断演变。

如今，大多数360 Rain机器还可以施用液态肥料，如硼、硫或微量元素，或液态粪肥。它们将肥料带状施入根区，与水混合。

"我们可以在这些养分的使用上非常高效，"360 Rain美国东部销售经理Loren Weaver说，并补充说目前50%到60%的机器用于奶牛和养猪场。几乎每台机器都在随水施用某种养分。

360 Rain系统旨在根据需要将水和养分直接施用到植物根部。"我们可以在用水方面非常高效，"360 Rain美国东部销售经理Loren Weaver说。（Holly Spangler）

该机器携带3000英尺长的3英寸软管，从一个连接点即可覆盖200英亩，这意味着它可以在中心 pivot 灌溉系统不太适用的不规则形状田块中进行灌溉。该公司声称，360 Rain比中心 pivot 灌溉系统节水40%，因为它不会因蒸发而损失水分。

相关阅读：条带耕作如何让一位农民从怀疑者变成信徒

该机器实际上不会在地头转弯；它会反向行驶，沿同一路线倒退并在途中收回软管。它使用GPS技术自主运行，基于种植期间记录的田块信息。它可以在单次加油后24/7连续运行长达30天。

"该机器设计为可适应30英寸行距，因此它会与每次播种机作业路线相交，并沿该主干道双向行驶，从而覆盖100%的田块，"Weaver说。

按照200加仑/分钟的泵送速率和约977,000加仑的水量计算，该机器大约需要三天半的时间才能在80英亩的田块上施用略低于半英寸的水。

Weaver报告称，该公司在40个州和加拿大都有机器，主要集中在俄亥俄州、印第安纳州和威斯康星州的奶牛养殖区。（360 Rain）

Weaver将360 Rain机器描述为一种"自适应施用系统"，可用于任何作物，施用从奶牛和猪粪肥到消化液和渗滤液的各种产品。

"任何这些产品都可以混入水流中施用，"他说，并补充说水和养分都可以变量施用。

**投资回报**

总体而言，Weaver表示该机器平均可带来40到60蒲式耳的产量增长，具体取决于地点和土壤类型。较轻的土壤或沙质、易干旱的土壤比降雨规律地区较重土壤的反应更为显著。他发现，即使在传统灌溉较少的更北部地区，农民仍然可以获得可观的产量增长。

"看看密歇根州南部的Borderview农场。他田块的一侧是较轻的土壤，另一侧是较重的土壤。在较轻的一侧，他获得了87蒲式耳的增长，在较重的土壤上，他获得了约42蒲式耳的增长，"Weaver说。

相关阅读："离不开它"：如何最大化氮肥施用效果

该公司声称其360 Rain机器比中心 pivot 灌溉系统节水40%，因为它不会因蒸发而损失水分。（360 Rain）

该机器的基本价格超过20万美元，Weaver估计如果农民用于施用粪肥，将在两到四年内实现投资回报。如果仅用于灌溉和养分施用，可能需要五年。

当然，产品本身也很重要。该机器在施用猪粪时特别有效，当养分如此容易获得时，回报非常显著。Weaver说，当他们在整个生长季节用四到五次猪粪施用配合水来"勺喂"作物时，他们看到了"非常非常好的结果"。

"相比之下，比如说，在秋季施用每英亩4,000加仑的猪粪。到了春天，作物只能获得大约一半的养分，"他解释说。

这意味着该机器还减少了养分流入水源的损失，并且由于根据需要直接将水施用到根部，实现了特别高效的用水。农民还可以在整个生长季节每周进行组织采样，并相应地调整肥料混合物。

360 Rain机器可通过当地经销商购买。
